content:
maria: Heads-up — since the 02:00 firmware push to south2 we've seen ~40% of new PXE boots fail and serial consoles dropping after ~10s. GPU provisioning backlog climbing, currently ~78 pending pods. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:
cheng: seeing same. logs show repeated 'ttyAMA0: disconnected' on the BMC side, then node moves to provisioning backoff.
dmitri: deploy-bot reported rollout completed to 240 nodes at 02:12 — payload v2.3.0-bmc-micro. Might be correlated.
infra-bot: firmware-rollout deploy-bot v2.3.0-bmc-micro completed for south2 (240 nodes), start 2029-11-02T02:05Z.
james: quick check — can you paste the last 20 lines of the serial log from one of affected hosts?
maria: paste: ```
[    4.123456] BMC: serial: drop TX
[    4.124000] ipmi_si: failed to open /dev/ttyAMA0
[    5.001234] EFI: SecureBoot: Toggle detected: Disabled -> Enabled
[    5.002000] UEFI: variable 'SetupMode' set
[   10.789111] console: ttyAMA0 hung for 10s, resetting
```
cheng: interesting — the UEFI variable flip to SetupMode/secureboot looks suspicious. secure boot toggles shouldn't be part of a BMC microcode push.
dmitri: confirmed on two different machines: nvram variable 'SecureBoot' flips to 1 during post-BMC-init. Could be our provisioning agent writing vars after a late-stage reboot.
james: mitigation options: 1) pause rollout and roll back BMC image to v2.2.7; 2) add a short delay in the provisioning agent to wait for BMC console; 3) route new provisioning requests to eu-west until south2 stabilizes. Cost impact: routing to eu-west increases egress and spot-burst cost estimate ~$3.2k/day at current load.
maria: can we hotfix the provisioning agent today? adding a wait won't undo the secureboot flip though.
cheng: short-term: I'll pause the remaining canary batches and set the rollout to manual. Infra-bot: cancel remaining rollout batches for v2.3.0 in south2.
infra-bot: action accepted — rollout paused. Remaining batches set to manual.
dmitri: runbook check: if nodes flip SecureBoot=1 and don't PXE, we can force nvram reset with ipmi raw or use `efibootmgr --nvram-erase` during rescue. Risky at scale.
james: I tried ipmitool on one node: `ipmitool -H bmc1.south2 -U redwood -P **** raw 0x30 0x70 0x0b 0x00` — it cleared the device serial pipe and console came back.
maria: nice. Can we script a safe probe: attempt ipmitool raw clear on nodes in provisioning queue and if console responds mark for reprovision? Estimate ~6m/node.
cheng: automation okay but be conservative — do a 10-node canary of ipmitool-based clears first. Also add a detector to flag sudden UEFI variable writes in console logs.
dmitri: I'll coordinate with firmware team. If root cause is BMC firmware writing to host nvram via platform-specific vendor hooks we need to revert. Opening issue infra/firmware#3421.
james: for capacity: moving 40 pending GPUs to eu-west now (manual burst) to keep customer SLAs. Oncall FYI — costs will spike.
maria: thanks. Action items: 1) cheng pause rollout (done), 2) dmitri open firmware issue (done), 3) james burst eu-west cap and run 10-node ipmitool canary, 4) infra-bot tag affected nodes for nvram-erase remediation. Keep thread updates short. :thumbsup:
